title: Group convergence on a shared downtime pick — venue voting, resolution-order logic, and cross-session unlocks
summary: When several players independently pick the same discretionary activity (the flagship case: Night Out), detect the convergence, hand the group a shared sub-choice of where to go, resolve it by vote under one of several selection shapes (one / an order / a subset / a subset in order), and let some venues stay locked until the group has already resolved others.
description:
Ingram's own framing, verbatim, from a downtime-mechanics riff: 'Let's say that three members of the group decide to "go for a night out", they pick the same activity as a choice. We could then provide those three players with choices of where to go and then resolve the event that gets the most votes for it. We could build in logic to support cases where it's pick one to resolve, pick an order to resolve, pick which to resolve, pick which and in what order to resolve to cover all cases. We could also include logic which means that if the group doesn't do A then they can't do D later on.'

This is new mechanical territory — nothing existing covers it. The Time Economy as designed (config.json's timeEconomy, ux-doctrine.md §7a's day ring) models each player's quarter/slice picks individually: 'eligibility' is about one player's own competing options within their own day, never about what happens when several players land on the SAME option. Night Out (design/downtime-activities.md §2 — clubbing/karaoke, −1 Bleed + a circumstance bonus, one of the proposed named rest types under the still-open rest-activity-roster question) is the obvious flagship case: it's flavoured as an inherently social, group-shaped activity, but as currently specified it resolves as an individual pick with no mechanism at all for what happens when three pilots pick it the same evening.

Four pieces, as given:
1. CONVERGENCE DETECTION — recognising that multiple players chose the same top-level discretionary option in the same quarter, which nothing in the current slice/quarter model checks for.
2. GROUP SUB-CHOICE — once convergence is detected, the converged players get a shared secondary decision (where specifically to go) rather than each resolving independently.
3. A GENERAL VOTE-RESOLUTION FRAMEWORK, named explicitly as needing to cover four distinct shapes: pick ONE winner; pick an ORDER (a full sequence); pick WHICH subset (multiple winners, unordered); pick WHICH subset AND IN WHAT ORDER. Framed generally enough to read as a reusable resolution mechanism rather than a Night-Out-only rule.
4. CROSS-INSTANCE PREREQUISITE GATING — 'if the group doesn't do A then they can't do D later on': venue options aren't independent one-shot flavour picks, they form a dependency chain that (on the most natural reading of 'later on') persists across separate Night Outs over the course of the campaign. This is the part with the most design weight — it turns Night Out from a one-shot bonus vending machine into a small persistent progression track the group builds by returning to it. That matters because design/strategy-and-downtime-design.md §6 (written the same day as this idea) names exactly this failure mode and its fix: 'an option that pays a bonus and touches nothing else on the menu is a vending machine, not a choice' — a gated venue chain is precisely 'interacting with something else on the menu.'

Recorded as a wishlist item — the whether-to-build, the resolution-mode mechanics, and the gating structure are all open.
sourceContext: Ingram, a follow-up 'new idea' message in the same session as the afterschool-club and road-network-routing wishlist items.
openSubQuestions: Is this Night-Out-specific, or a general convergence/voting mechanism meant to apply anywhere multiple players land on the same discretionary pick?
Does convergence require an exact match (all chose 'Night Out' specifically), or does it also cover adjacent/compatible picks?

What happens to a player who picks Night Out alone, with nobody converging — solo resolution as design/downtime-activities.md §2 already specifies, or does going alone lose something the group version grants?
Are the four resolution-mode shapes (one / order / subset / subset-in-order) chosen per venue-set by the GM ahead of time, or does the system need to support switching between them dynamically?

Is the A-then-D prerequisite a permanent unlock (once the group visits A, D is available on every future Night Out) or a per-outing gate (this evening only)? 'Later on' reads as the former, which is the more interesting and more work.
Does gating care WHO was in the group that unlocked it — must the same players return, or does any prior group visit to A unlock D for the whole party regardless of who was there?
